instruction: View capabilities for all suid binaries
Audit all files with file capabilities
Find any file with any capability

output:
cat > /tmp/cap-audit.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
echo "=== Capability Audit ==="
echo "Files with capabilities:"
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null
echo ""
echo "Running processes with special caps:"
for pid in /proc/[0-9]*; do
    pid=${pid#/proc/}
    caps=$(cat /proc/$pid/status 2>/dev/null | grep CapEff | awk '{print $2}')
    if [ "$caps" ] && [ "$caps" != "0000000000000000" ]; then
        echo "PID $pid: $(cat /proc/$pid/comm 2>/dev/null) -> $(capsh --decode=$caps 2>/dev/null)"
    fi
done
EOF
bash /tmp/cap-audit.sh

instruction: Find SUID binaries without file caps
output: find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null | while read f; do getcap "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -q . || echo "$f (no cap)"; done

instruction: Check if capabilities are enabled on system
Check kernel config for file capabilities
Verify capabilities in kernel boot params
Check if user namespaces are enabled

output:
cat > /usr/local/bin/audit-caps.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
REPORT="/tmp/cap-report-$(date +%Y%m%d).txt"
echo "Capability Audit Report - $(date)" > "$REPORT"
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null >> "$REPORT"
echo "" >> "$REPORT"
echo "=== Dangerous Capabilities Check ===" >> "$REPORT"
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei 'cap_sys_admin|cap_dac_override|cap_sys_ptrace' >> "$REPORT"
echo "Report saved to $REPORT"
EOF
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/audit-caps.sh
